prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-18, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-18):
| Current ratio           | 0.94 |
| Retained earnings       | 21,891M |
| Current liabilities     | 9,428M |
| Current assets          | 8,827M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 36,034M |
| Total liabilities       | 50,185M |
| Total assets            | 86,783M |
| EBIT / operating income | 467M |
| Revenue                 | 5,013M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows modest profitability (EBIT ~9% of revenue) with solid equity and sizable retained earnings, but a current ratio below 1 indicates liquidity pressure. Leverage is moderate-to-high (debt ~58% of assets, debt to equity ~1.4), suggesting some refinancing risk if earnings deteriorate. On balance, this aligns with a lower-investment-grade rating rather than outright investment-grade.

DECISION: BBB-
